value_unit: provider-scoped rate-limit memory shared across distinct mutation actions
separability: standalone coordination invariant
decision_rationale: The earlier LumiNet convergence remembered 429 cooldown by action. Final cross-wave comparison shows provider quotas can span several mutation endpoints, so action-only memory still permits cross-action quota hammering. LumiNet independently generalizes the AGPL evidence into an explicit secret-free RateLimitScope shared only by mutations that declare a common provider quota boundary.
invariant: provider throttling learned by one declared action suppresses other actions in the same provider scope without globally suppressing unrelated providers
negative_invariant: scope keys must never contain URLs, credentials or request payloads, and scope sharing must never relax per-action retry safety class

license_note: AGPL evidence only; independently rederived; no donor code copied

value_unit: bounded per-provider mutation concurrency with fail-closed coordinator capacity
separability: standalone coordination bound
decision_rationale: The donor constrains outbound request concurrency at its provider HTTP client. LumiNet needs the stronger cross-call mutation invariant at the retry coordinator itself: declared provider scopes have a bounded in-flight gate and the coordinator refuses to allocate unbounded scope state before mutation I/O.
invariant: at most the declared bounded number of mutations may be in flight in one provider scope and coordinator scope cardinality is bounded
negative_invariant: capacity exhaustion must fail before emitting a mutation; waiting callers must remain cancellable; bounds must not coalesce semantically different mutations
migration_impact: additive bounded coordination; default in-flight limit for existing policies
license_note: AGPL evidence only; independently rederived; no donor code copied

value_unit: de-synchronized local retry backoff while preserving authoritative Retry-After
separability: standalone retry timing invariant
decision_rationale: Deterministic exponential sleeps can synchronize callers after a shared outage. LumiNet adds equal jitter only to locally chosen exponential backoff while treating provider Retry-After as authoritative and exact; this avoids herd re-entry without second-guessing provider recovery instructions.
invariant: local retry delay is randomized within a bounded interval while explicit provider delay is not jittered
negative_invariant: jitter must never extend beyond configured maximum or alter Retry-After semantics
migration_impact: timing-only hardening within existing bounded retry contract
license_note: AGPL donor behavior used as negative evidence; no donor code copied

value_unit: restart-safe durable configuration generation preventing validator ABA
separability: standalone persistence invariant
decision_rationale: Caddy demonstrates that configuration validators must identify the active representation. A process-local counter would reset on restart and permit ABA acceptance of an old cfg-1. LumiNet therefore persists a monotonic config generation, migrates legacy files, and advances externally edited files that reuse an old generation.
invariant: the committed generation survives restart and never rolls backward for the canonical config
negative_invariant: legacy migration or external edits must not permit reuse of a previously authoritative stale validator
migration_impact: legacy config files gain _revision on first authoritative load; generation is internal metadata
license_note: Apache-2.0 test oracle; implementation is target-native durable generation rather than donor hash representation

value_unit: copy-on-write secret references composed transactionally with config publication
separability: inseparable from canonical config commit boundary
decision_rationale: Once live config mutation became transactional, the final pass found a target-local cross-store hole: overwriting a referenced secret before the config file commit could make the old file resolve to a new secret after a failed save. LumiNet stages changed secrets under new references, rolls them back on failed config commit, publishes the config, then best-effort retires superseded refs.
invariant: a failed config commit cannot mutate the meaning of the previously committed secret reference; successful publication owns the new refs before old refs are retired
negative_invariant: no currently referenced secret may be overwritten pre-commit and cleanup failure after commit must not make committed config unavailable
migration_impact: secret updates allocate a fresh native reference; obsolete refs retired after durable commit
license_note: transaction principle is permissive donor evidence; secret implementation is independent LumiNet design

value_unit: deduplication queue examined as a mutation-coalescing candidate and converted into a payload-identity guardrail
separability: standalone semantic constraint
decision_rationale: A unique queue is useful when element identity truly defines equivalent work. Remote mutations cannot be safely coalesced merely because they share an action or provider scope: two calls may carry different payloads. LumiNet therefore shares cooldown/capacity only; replay/coalescing remains governed by explicit idempotency and reconciliation semantics.
invariant: provider-scope coordination controls timing/capacity but never asserts payload equivalence
negative_invariant: never deduplicate arbitrary mutations by action name, provider scope or endpoint alone

decision_rationale: InviZible and Firewalla demonstrate substantial Unix firewall/DNS-leak policy surfaces, but directly importing iptables machinery would create a second privileged host-network authority outside LumiNet’s durable snapshot/apply/verify/recover/rollback transaction. The final convergence therefore keeps Unix DNS-leak protection truthfully unsupported until it can be modeled as a first-class HostNetworkChange with reversible state capture and verification.

negative_invariant: never advertise Unix DNS-leak protection or execute peer iptables rules through an untracked side authority

migration_impact: none; preserves truthful unsupported behavior pending a transactionally reversible implementation
